You can follow the action from the match, and all of today’s Serie A fixtures, on our Live Blog. item.title: Fernando Alonso 'beyond frustration' after engine issue in F1 Mexico GP qualifying
item.description: Motorsport photo Fernando Alonso stated that his “frustration is beyond imagination” after a power unit problem caused an early end to his qualifying for the Formula 1 Mexico Grand Prix. The Aston Martin driver took 18th with only one flying lap as his AMR26 ground to a halt through the stadium section of Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez with 11 minutes left in Q1. It was a gut-wrenching moment for the two-time champion who was fastest of 11 drivers at the time, before eventually dropping into the elimination zone and 0.387s off Q2. “Huge problems with temperatures for everybody,” said Alonso. “So, when you start at the back, there is no way you can follow cars closely or something like that. “There is not much we can do. I think we lost a big opportunity. So, yeah, frustration is beyond imagination. But this is the story of the year.” Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing Alonso was therefore denied a third progression to Q2 in five rounds having enjoyed an upturn in form since Aston Martin’s upgrades for Budapest and Zandvoort either side of the summer break. So when asked whether even Q3 could have been possible in Mexico, Alonso, whose team-mate Lance Stroll qualified 20th, said: “Probably difficult. “We were P12, P13, P11, so we were in the window. If we put a good lap, maybe it was possible, but I think that was probably too optimistic. Maybe P13, P12 was our position today.” Read Also: Liam Lawson disqualified from F1 qualifying in Mexico – here's why To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: 'All the qualities of leader': Yuvraj Singh backs Abhishek Sharma for India captaincy, inclusion in ODIs
item.description: Former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh believes Abhishek Sharma has the qualities to become a leader and could captain the national team in the future. Abhishek is yet to captain an IPL side. He was named Sunrisers Hyderabad's vice-captain earlier this year, while Ishan Kishan took charge during the first half of the tournament in the absence of Pat Cummins. Yuvraj, who has mentored Abhishek and shares a close bond with the left-handed batter, pointed to the way he encourages younger players as one of the signs of his leadership qualities. He also believes captaining an IPL team can help a player prepare for the India captaincy. “Well, it’s too early to say whether he has the makings of a captain, but I feel he has all the qualities of a leader. I think he encourages the younger guys in state cricket as well. I love the way he encourages Sooryavanshi, puts his hand on his shoulder and motivates him. I think that’s a good sign of a senior leader, whatever you want to call it," Yuvraj was quoted as saying by Cricbuzz. “If you want to captain India one day, I think it’s important to captain your IPL side. That gives you the kind of confidence you need to lead India. I’m sure time will tell whether he is capable of doing it. If it’s in his destiny, I’m sure he’ll get the opportunity. If not, then so be it. But I’m sure he’ll finish as a great white-ball player, whether he becomes captain or not.” Yuvraj, who was part of India's 2007 T20 World Cup and 2011 ODI World Cup-winning teams, also backed Abhishek's inclusion in the national ODI squad. He said the batter's consistent performances in white-ball cricket should be considered when selectors assess his chances. “Whether he has scored 35, 100 or 31, 100, the point is that he has been performing consistently in white-ball cricket for a very long time. What more he needs to do to get into the ODI squad, I don't know. Maybe he needs to contribute more with his bowling and fielding. But that will only happen if he gets an opportunity to play," he said. Yuvraj acknowledged the competition for places in the Indian team but said Abhishek would need an opportunity to show what he can do in the 50-over format. He also referred to Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's performances as an example of a young player earning his place in the T20 squad. “There are always areas to improve, and I think unless you give a player a chance, where is he going to showcase his talent? I understand that the situation is difficult right now because there is so much competition for places in the squad, along with some big names. But look at Sooryavanshi. He was brilliant and made his own place in the T20 squad. If you feel that Abhishek is performing brilliantly at the moment, then somewhere you have to make a place for him to play 50-over cricket until the World Cup.”

item.title: Lewis Hall is winning the World Cup for England at left-back, while still a Newcastle United player
item.description: Lewis Hall and Jude Bellingham England In a possible future version of this football world, Lewis Hall is winning the World Cup for England at left-back, while still a Newcastle United player. At right midfield in the same team is Lewis Miley, Hall’s Newcastle teammate. They have transferred their unique understanding at club level to the international arena. However, in another not-so-impossible future, it’s easy to see them both as the next players that Newcastle United cash in on. So, let’s forget about Fantasy Island, and in the interim, let’s see what the two of them could do in a Newcastle side reinvented tactically and positionally – while we’ve still got time. I’ll start with Lewis Hall. For a couple of games last season, Newcastle’s absolute best player, even with our former midfield talisman Bruno on the pitch, was Lewis Hall. From left-back, he ran the game. He moved forward into what would have been called a half-back position – just ahead of the central defenders but relatively narrow. From there his ability to tackle and pass gave a new dimension to the creative thrust of the midfield. The central defenders would split left and right and one of the midfield trio would drop back into a back three temporarily to accommodate this switch. All football tactics come down to freeing up some potential so you have more or better options than your opponents. It was obvious that Eddie Howe allowed this move or was even encouraging it. It gave Newcastle a new dimension, allowing the attackers to concentrate on attack, and to make defence a much more attacking option, without necessarily sacrificing solidity. I noticed Howe also seemed to be favouring Miley at right-back, and that he seemed to be slowly pushing him into a similar right-back/right-half hybrid. In the world of number sixes, number eights and number 10s, it’s worth explaining what a half-back used to be. The half-back was a player who tackled hard, broke up opposition attacks and linked defence to attack. At Newcastle, Jimmy Scoular was a legendary example, while Billy Bremner at Leeds offers a more familiar illustration of the combination of aggression, intelligence and passing ability. Modern football has divided many of those responsibilities between holding midfielders, central defenders and inverted full-backs. item.title: Offensive snap counts from FSU's loss to Clemson
item.description: The FSU Seminoles once again relied on just a core group of offensive players in their 36-24 loss to the Clemson Tigers on Saturday night. While FSU lacked depth at certain positions entering the season, injuries have forced them to rely on younger players at several key spots. You felt Ousmane Kromah's absence in the backfield, where Quintrevion Wisner and Amari Thomas combined for just 44 yards on 14 attempts, averaging 3.1 yards per carry. The wide receiver corps was also tested, with Duce Robinson suffering an injury and having to leave the game. They did get several solid performances from Jasen Lopez and Micahi Danzy, but would have loved to have their top option during their comeback attempt. item.title: 4 bold predictions for Broncos’ game vs. Chiefs
item.description: Despite a crushing defeat at the hands of the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 1, the Denver Broncos have put themselves in position to take over the AFC West division lead at the midway point of the season if they can return the favor on Sunday. The Broncos will host the Chiefs on Sunday in a key game for both teams. This time it will be played in Denver and this time, the two teams have very different momentum behind them. While the Broncos have won their last three games, the Chiefs are coming off a 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks last Sunday night. A win puts the Broncos at 6-2 with a favorable schedule in front of them for the rest of the season. This is a game they need to find a way to win, leading to these four bold predictions. Broncos' Week 8 bold predictions 1. Jonah Coleman hits the century mark Jonah Coleman has carried the ball in just two games for the Broncos this season, rushing for 39 and 54 yards in those two games, respectively. That puts him at 93 yards rushing on 19 carries for the season. But things have shifted in Denver's backfield and he is clearly the team's most effective runner. The Broncos will feed him the ball in this game and he will outdo his entire seasonal output in this game, breaking the 100-yard rushing mark for the first time in his professional career. 2. Evan Engram scores again Evan Engram has scored just one touchdown this season while catching just 13 passes in seven games. He had four of those receptions and that touchdown in Week 1 against the Chiefs. In this game, with the Broncos missing Pat Bryant and potentially Jaylen Waddle at wide receiver, along with one of their better receiving options in running back RJ Harvey , Engram will get his chances and make the most of them, finding the end zone against the Chiefs for a second time this season. 3. Brandon Jones does it again This will be two predictions in one. In Week 1, the Broncos, for as badly as they played, had a great chance to turn things around in the third quarter when Brandon Jones intercepted a pass thrown by Patrick Mahomes and returned it 24 yards to the Chiefs' 5-yard line. Trailing 21-7 at the time, the Broncos had a chance to cut it to a one-score game. Instead, a holding penalty against Bryant and a sack of Bo Nix allowed the Chiefs to escape by just giving up a field goal. Sunday, Jones will get Mahomes again. With the Chiefs trailing late, the Broncos will get quick pressure on Mahomes, who will make an ill-advised throw that lands in the arms of Jones. This time, it will seal a victory for the Broncos. Broncos win, 20-14 . Social : Follow Broncos Wire on Facebook and Twitter/X ! This article originally appeared on Broncos Wire: 4 bold predictions for Broncos’ game vs. Chiefs

Braces from Raphinha and Lamine Yamal and a goal apiece from Fermin Lopez and Anthony Gordon helped Flick’s men secure the three points. However, the game also highlighted the situation of one player who has been struggling for minutes recently. Despite Flick resting Pedri in the second half, Gavi remained an unused substitute. Barcelona’s midfield is packed with quality, and the competition for places is starting to affect the young Spaniard. According to Diario AS , the 22-year-old has started just two matches this season, accumulating a paltry total of 191 minutes. He has not played a single minute in the last two games against Real Madrid or Alaves and continues to wait for an opportunity. Gavi slipping down Barcelona’s midfield hierarchy Only four Barcelona first-team players have played fewer minutes: Alejandro Balde (116), Frenkie de Jong (98), Brian Farinas (90) and Roony Bardghji (0). Gavi’s Barcelona career is going seemingly nowhere. (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images) Gavi started the opening league match against Elche, partnering Marc Bernal in midfield. He had to wait almost two months for his next start against Getafe. His situation has been complicated by Barcelona being spoilt for choice in that position. Rodri, Pedri, Bernal and Frenkie de Jong all seem to be ahead of him for the deeper midfield role. In attacking midfield, Fermin Lopez and Dani Olmo rotate, leaving Gavi with nowhere to go. Flick’s public backing has not brought opportunities Flick has consistently spoken very highly of Gavi, his ability and the quality and mentality he can bring to midfield. However, despite the public backing, the German manager has been unable to find a role for the Spaniard in his team. Gavi needs to show Flick why he deserves more opportunities in the coming weeks. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) It is a shame to see Gavi, a fan favourite, reach this point in his career after the incredible start he had in the first team. Once undroppable from the starting XI, the 22-year-old is barely getting opportunities to prove himself, even off the bench. Successive injury problems have really taken the sting out of Gavi’s footballing career, and he needs to start showing some improvement. The upcoming fixtures could see the Spaniard get an opportunity, and he needs to show Hansi Flick why he deserves more minutes. The only way for Gavi to prove a point is through his actions, and it remains to be seen how he fares in the coming weeks.

item.title: Steph Curry breaking Luka Doncic’s ankles prompts 1985 cult classic movie-inspired reaction from Jimmy Butler
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Jimmy Butler is not ready to let Luka Doncic forget what Steph Curry did to him when the Golden State Warriors faced off against the Los Angeles Lakers on Friday. In the third quarter of the game, Curry had the ball in his hands, and as always, one expects great things when the four-time champion is in control. With the Warriors trying to put on a scoring run, Curry pulled off a move that saw Doncic drop to the floor. The 38-year-old then drained the three-pointer and celebrated as the Chase Center went berserk after seeing what they witnessed. Speaking about the ankle-breaker, Curry said: “I didn’t expect it to get that n***, but it was one of those you gotta kind of keep your composure. And I remember James Harden had to do like the shimmy to get himself going back in the day. I don’t know, I haven’t been that open in a long time.” Curry scored 31 on the night and helped the Warriors grab a dominant 112-95 win. Jimmy Butler, who was not even playing, trolled Doncic with his post on Instagram about the ankle breaker. Jimmy Butler posts AI video of famous scene from the Last Dragon movie Butler is not the one who gives up any chance to have a laugh. Having found his moment, Butler went on Instagram and posted an AI video from the Last Dragon movie. Curry’s AI face was Bruce Leroy from the 1985 movie, The Last Dragon. During the scene, Curry is asked: “”Alright Leroy, who’s the one-and-only Master?” to this, Leroy responds, “I am!” A bystander, who was played by Doncic’s AI face, then said, “Holy s***!” Butler then proceeded to post a slow-motion video of the moment Curry dropped Doncic to his ankles. He also posted a picture of Doncic on the floor and then went on to add other pictures from the game. He has been cheering the team from the sidelines as he prepares to make his return to the court. There is reportedly a belief that he will come back in February, but until then, expect similar videos of him trolling the opponents. item.title: One year later, Luciano Spalletti is setting the wrong record at Juventus
item.description: One year later, Luciano Spalletti is setting the wrong record at Juventus Luciano Spalletti was appointed Juventus manager on 30 October 2025 and has now spent a year on the bench. However, the results have not matched the expectations that he or the club had when he arrived. Juventus believed they had appointed one of the best Italian coaches available, and Spalletti’s previous record supports that view. He enjoyed success at clubs including AS Roma and Napoli, winning the Scudetto with the latter in 2023. A difficult first year Spalletti did not join Juventus at a time when the club were performing at their best. He arrived with the task of trying to save the team, but his position could come under pressure in the coming weeks if results do not improve. Although there have been some improvements under his management, Juventus have ended his first year in eighth place in Serie A with 14 points. As reported by Calciomercato , they are 11 points behind the leaders and six points outside the top four after nine league matches. That is their worst distance from the top six since the introduction of three points for a win after nine league matches. For a club of Juventus’ stature, the situation is far from satisfactory and raises questions about the progress made under Spalletti. (Photo by Alessandro Sabattini/Getty Images) Pressure on Spalletti Spalletti is aware of the demands at Juventus and the importance of delivering results. The club expected him to improve their performances and help them compete at the highest level, but the early returns have fallen short of those expectations. Juventus remain a major club in Italian football, but their current league position reflects the difficulties they have faced. The gap to the top four is significant, and the team need to improve quickly if they are to climb the table and challenge for European qualification. Spalletti’s first year has been challenging, and the pressure on him is likely to increase if results do not pick up. Juventus need a strong response in the coming weeks, as the club looks to move away from their current position and get back to competing at the top of Serie A.

item.title: Bayern Munich’s Ismael Saibari could be out three months
item.description: (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bayern Munich will be without Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry following Saturday’s 2-2 draw against Borussia Dortmund, with both players picking up injuries during Der Klassiker. According to the club’s official website , Saibari suffered a tear to the syndesmotic ligament in his right ankle and has already undergone surgery. The injury is particularly concerning, with Bild (via @iMiaSanMia ) reporting that the midfielder is expected to be sidelined for at least three months. Gnabry, meanwhile, sustained a muscular injury in his left hamstring. Bayern Munich has confirmed the diagnosis but has not yet provided a specific timeline for his return. There is also still no word on the extent of the injury that caused Michael Olise to leave the game. It is another frustrating setback for the Bavarians, who are already dealing with several injury concerns. Losing Saibari for such an extended period is especially disappointing, while Gnabry’s absence further limits the team’s options in attack. The timing could hardly be worse as Bayern Munich enters another demanding stretch of the season. item.title: Serie A | Como 1-0 Venezia: Da Cunha penalty keeps Fabregas’ side flying
item.description: Serie A | Como 1-0 Venezia: Da Cunha penalty keeps Fabregas’ side flying Lucas Da Cunha’s first-half penalty gave Como a narrow 1-0 win over bottom side Venezia, despite an inspired display from Filip Stanković and a VAR reprieve at the other end. Como went into the game fifth on 20 points after Tuesday’s 3-1 win at Torino, the best start in the club’s history, and with a Champions League trip to Lens to come on Wednesday. Cesc Fàbregas was without Moise Kean, who faces around five weeks out, as well as Assane Diao, Jesús Rodríguez, Trevoh Chalobah and Addai. Mattia Liberali returned to the bench after injury, and Jean Butez started in goal. Venezia were bottom with three points after losing 2-0 to Inter in midweek. Davide Nicola was still without Bartol Franjić and Andrea Adorante, and he handed starts to Lion Lauberbach and Gianluca Busio. See how it all unfolded on the Liveblog. Como dominated the ball from the start, with 76% possession in the opening 18 minutes, but found Venezia’s five-man defence hard to break down. Kaiki headed over from a Luis Milla corner, Tasos Douvikas had a shot blocked after a Nico Paz through ball, and Martin Baturina blazed over from the edge of the box. Stanković was soon busy. The Venezia goalkeeper got down well to keep out Da Cunha’s low drive towards the bottom corner, then needed treatment after the save. COMO, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Nico Paz of Como 1907 runs with the ball under pressure from Kike Perez of Venezia FC during the Serie A match between Como 1907 and Venezia FC at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Como, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) Tale of two penalties as Venezia denied by VAR Venezia thought they had a penalty on 28 minutes, when Milla was penalised for handball. After an on-field review, Maria Sole Ferrieri Caputi overturned her decision. Como kept pushing. Stanković produced a superb reflex save to deny Marc-Oliver Kempf’s effort from a rebound, Milla fired just over from the edge of the area, and Douvikas headed narrowly wide from Baturina’s cross. The breakthrough came moments later. Juan Jesus slid in on Douvikas inside the box and was booked for conceding the penalty, and Da Cunha sent a left-footed spot kick into the top-left corner on 43 minutes. Venezia almost levelled before the break, but Thórir Helgason’s shot from the right side of the area flew just past the far post. Stanković kept Venezia in the game after the restart, tipping away Baturina’s curling effort after the Croatian had danced past several challenges. Nicola made changes before the hour, bringing on Kike Pérez and John Yeboah, then Toma Bašić and Richie Sagrado. The substitutes livened Venezia up. Yeboah went close twice from distance, and Kike Pérez fired high and wide. Yan Couto had the best chance to settle it at the other end, dragging a shot from the edge of the area just wide. item.title: Dortmund chief Cramer: No pressure to sell despite financial losses
item.description: Borussia Dortmund's Jobe Bellingham scores a goal that was later disallowed for Bayern Munich goalkeeper Jonas Urbig being obstructed during the German Bundesliga soccer match between FC Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Dortmund chief Cramer: No pressure to sell despite financial losses») Tom Weller/dpa Borussia Dortmund chief Carsten Cramer says the Bundesliga side will not be forced to sell their best players despite a loss in the double-digit millions in the last financial year. The German club reported a consolidated annual loss of €21.7 million ($24.3 million) for the 2025-26 financial year. In the previous year, the listed club had made a profit of €6.7 million. "I am very, very confident that we will be able to keep our squad together in the summer," Cramer told broadcaster Sport1 on Sunday. "We are financially sound at the core and are also working to ensure that we are not forced into selling." But some player sales may still occur in the coming windows. "If there are economic opportunities, then we will think about them. I do not want to rule anything out. But we are not doing this to constantly sell players. Instead, we want to develop further on the pitch," the 57-year-old said. Dortmund are level on points at the top of the Bundesliga with rivals Bayern Munich following a 2-2 draw between the sides in Bavaria on Saturday. Only eight games have been played this term. The Black and Yellows last won the Bundesliga under Jürgen Klopp in 2012. Bayern have taken every title since then except for 2024 when unbeaten Bayer Leverkusen pulled off a major surprise. Cramer even left open the possibility of January arrivals for Niko Kovač's squad "The fact is we are able to act at any time. And if there was something to do, we would certainly be able to do it," he stressed.

item.title: Yamaha pulls out of Qatar MotoGP over 'Middle East situation'
item.description: France's 2021 MotoGP world champion Fabio Quartararo will miss the Qatar race after Yamaha said it would not compete there (Paul Crock) Yamaha said on Sunday it will not participate in next weekend's Qatar MotoGP, citing "the situation in the Middle East". Diplomatic efforts to end the Middle East war have been punctuated by repeated threats from the United States and Israel to resume bombardments of Iran. The war began on February 28 with joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran, which retaliated by targeting, among others, Gulf countries allied with Washington. Yamaha issued a statement after Sunday's Malaysian MotoGP saying they would not be taking the risk of going to Qatar. "Yamaha has not identified sufficient grounds to change its existing company-wide travel restrictions," the Japanese manufacturer said. Yamaha's riders are France's Fabio Quartararo, the 2021 world champion, and Spaniard Alex Rins. Australia's Jack Miller, who rides for the Japanese operation's satellite team Yamaha-Pramac, will have been happy with the decision as he made clear his reluctance to travel to Qatar just before Yamaha issued their statement. "I have no desire to go," said Miller. "Just like everyone else. There are 19 (out of 22 riders) who do not want to go there. "I do not think we should ride in those conditions. We have been very clear about our position," added the 31-year-old, who has won four MotoGP's during his career. The MotoGP Group said it was "disappointed" by the decision and said that "Yamaha's non-participation also carries sporting implications". "While we recognise the team is subject to a broader corporate policy restricting travel to the Middle East, we do not believe this decision reflects the extensive assurances provided to all championship stakeholders," it said. MotoGP said talks with Qatari organisers and safety advisers had not flagged any reasons to change plans for the event. "We communicated that position, together with the latest available information, to all manufacturers and teams today and welcome the confirmation from the remainder of the grid that they will compete in Qatar, and we thank them for that commitment," the MotoGP Group said. There are just three races left in the season, starting in Qatar. Ducati's reigning seven-time world champion Marc Marquez won the race at Sepang and could clinch the title in Doha. According to reports, there was haggling behind the scenes in Sepang about whether teams would go to Qatar and it has been reported that anyone who did swerve next weekend's race would be penalised. - 'Standing their ground' - Sporting events in the Gulf have been affected by both the conflict with Iran and Saudi Arabia's clashes with the Houthis in Yemen.
